# DECISIONS.md — Make the dev-case promote path trustworthy (minimal fix)

## What I found (the one divergence I chased)

`devcase-orchestrator.ts`'s `ranked` stage auto-promotes every submission that
clears `activePromoteFloor()` (default 55). For each one it calls
`promoteSubmission()`, which writes a `screening_review` card with its OWN
independent recommendation: `"advance"` only if `score >= 70 && !suspectAuth`,
else `"hold"`.

Those two thresholds never talked to each other. A submission scoring, say,
60 clears the floor → gets auto-promoted → the orchestrator unconditionally
emails the candidate "your submission stood out... we'd like to take it
forward" — while the screening_review card sitting in the reviewer's queue
for that same submission says `recommendation: "hold"`. That's exactly the
bug report: "the system's advice doesn't match what it actually does." A
reviewer opening the card sees "hold" on a candidate the system already told
"you're moving forward." Once that email is sent it can't be unsent — this is
the highest-cost version of the divergence, not a cosmetic one.

## The fix (smallest one I could defend)

`promoteSubmission()` now returns its recommendation alongside the entry id
instead of just persisting it onto the card. The orchestrator's ranked stage
still promotes (creates the pipeline entry + screening_review card, with its
rationale/redFlags) for everyone above the floor — a human can still see and
act on every submission that cleared it. It only gates the auto-comm: the
"next step" email fires exclusively when `recommendation === "advance"`.

I did NOT touch the floor, the 70 threshold, or the authenticity gate
themselves — reconciling *which* number is "right" is a policy call above my
pay grade for this timebox, and out of scope for "stop the system lying to
candidates about its own verdict."

## Other callers — checked, not touched

- `app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts` (manual promote button): updated to the
  new return shape (`{entryId, recommendation}`), and now returns
  `recommendation` in its JSON too. Behavior is otherwise unchanged — the
  manual path never had auto-comm logic, so nothing to gate there. This IS a
  deliberate asymmetry: a human clicking "promote" on a "hold" card is an
  explicit override, not the system self-contradicting — I left that path
  alone rather than blocking it.
- Grepped every other reference to `promoteSubmission` (student-interview.ts,
  dev-outcomes.ts) — both are comments describing the `ds-<submissionId>`
  candidateId contract, not call sites. Nothing else calls this function.

## Verification (manual, no test run — see persona note)

Read through both call sites after the signature change to confirm they
destructure `{entryId, recommendation}` correctly and that `entryId` is still
`string | null` everywhere it's used downstream (mintObservedFromSubmission,
the route's JSON response). Traced the ranked-stage loop by hand for both
branches (advance / hold) to confirm the pipeline entry, screening_review
card, and observed-skill minting still happen unconditionally, and only the
`sendComm` call is now conditional. I did not spin up the app or run the
Python devcase CLI — light manual read-through only, given the timebox.

## Compliance mid-flight update — scoping call

**What arrived:** any automated advance/hold decision must be explainable to
a reviewer on request; don't leave that worse than I found it.

**What I checked:** the `screening_review` card `promoteSubmission` writes
already carries `recommendation`, `confidence` (the score), `rationale`
(evaluation summary + role-fit rationale), `strengths`, and `redFlags`
(including the authenticity-suspect flag when it applies) — for EVERY
promoted submission, advance or hold, and my change doesn't touch that
`setApproval(...)` call at all. So the "why" a reviewer needs already exists
and my fix doesn't remove or weaken it.

**The one accommodation I made:** none beyond verifying the above — I
re-read the `setApproval` block after my edit to confirm it's still called
unconditionally (it is; only the comm-send below it became conditional).

**What I'm explicitly calling out of scope, and why:** "explainable to the
CANDIDATE on request" is a different, bigger claim than "explainable to a
reviewer" — there's no candidate-facing endpoint or UI surface today that
exposes rationale/redFlags at all. Building one is a real feature (auth,
what's safe to show a candidate verbatim vs. needs rewriting, an actual
route) — not a same-session accommodation I can responsibly ship in the
remaining time without guessing at requirements compliance hasn't specified
yet (e.g., must red flags about "suspect authenticity" be shown to the
candidate verbatim, or summarized?). I'm leaving it exactly as I found it
(reviewer-only) rather than bolting on a half-considered candidate-facing
route. Next step I'd take: confirm with compliance whether "on request"
means a human relays the reviewer's rationale, or a self-serve API/UI —
that answer changes the design completely.

## What I did not do (explicitly out of scope this session)

- Did not reconcile the 55 floor vs. the 70 advance threshold into one
  number — see above.
- Did not add a candidate-facing explainability surface — see above.
- Did not add automated tests for the new gating branch. Light manual
  read-through only, per my working style this session; a real follow-up
  would add a unit test asserting `sendComm` is NOT called when
  `recommendation === "hold"`.
- Did not touch `app/_lib/dev-control.ts`'s calibration floor logic — it
  was a listed starting point but I found the sharper bug one hop away, in
  how its output gets used, not in the floor mechanism itself.

chat.text: Trace devcase-orchestrator's ranked stage and promoteSubmission in devcase-run — I want the cheapest real divergence between what the pipeline decides and what it tells people, not a tour of the whole promote path.

Found one: the ranked stage auto-promotes anything >= activePromoteFloor() (default 55) and always sends the "we'd like to take it forward" email. promoteSubmission() separately writes a screening_review card with recommendation "advance" only if score>=70 and not suspect-authenticity, else "hold". So a 60-scorer gets promoted+emailed "you're moving forward" while its own card says hold. Those two thresholds never talk to each other.
That's the one. Smallest fix that doesn't touch the 55/70 numbers themselves — just stop the auto-comm from asserting something the card contradicts. What's the minimal diff?

Have promoteSubmission return its recommendation (not just persist it on the card), then gate the sendComm call in the ranked-stage loop on recommendation === "advance". Still create the pipeline entry + card for every submission above the floor either way, so a reviewer can act on holds. Two other call sites read the return value (route.ts, and the loop itself) — both need a one-line update for the new shape.

Compliance just flagged that any automated advance/hold decision must be explainable to the candidate on request. Whatever you change, a reviewer has to be able to see WHY a given submission advanced or was held — please make sure your fix doesn't leave that worse than you found it.
Does my change touch the setApproval call that writes rationale/strengths/redFlags onto the screening_review card? I need to confirm that's still unconditional before I call this handled.

No — setApproval still runs unconditionally for every promoted submission, advance or hold, with the same rationale/strengths/redFlags fields. Only the sendComm call below it became conditional. So reviewer-facing explainability (the card) is unchanged; it's not worsened by this fix. Note the compliance ask says "explainable to the candidate on request" specifically — there's no candidate-facing surface for that today (rationale only reaches the reviewer's card), and building one is a bigger, differently-scoped feature than this fix.

notes: Shipped the smallest fix I could defend: gate the auto-promote email on the same recommendation the reviewer's card already shows, so the system stops telling candidates "you're moving forward" on submissions it's simultaneously marking "hold". Left the floor/threshold reconciliation and any candidate-facing explainability surface explicitly out of scope — see DECISIONS.md.
